cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Tax Machine plan next year's estimated tax payments for HANGS Construction Services.
It starts from last year's tax, and finds that HANGS counts as a large corporation, with stricter rules.
Next, this year's numbers: the first quarter's actual income, and a projection for the rest of the year.
Then the payments already made, and the client's email.
The company's fiscal year ends in June, not December.
One payment was filed under the wrong tax year.
Now it checks the official rules online: the due dates, the large corporation rules and the penalty rates.
Each rule is matched to the client's records.
The four payments fall due in October, December, March and June.
Then it works out the year's projected tax: about $71,000.
A large corporation can base only the first payment on last year's tax.
Taxing income as it is actually earned lowers the next payment.
That payment, due December 15, is about $18,300.
Every payment ties to the projected tax.
Last, it writes the payment plan and the workpapers behind it.

All done. The plan projects about $71,000 of tax for the year, with about $18,300 due December 15. Five items stay open, including an October payment filed under the wrong tax year. A person approves the plan; nothing has been paid yet.
Here are the results: about $18,300 due December 15, and five open items for a person to decide.
